R1C-bear-backcountry-0001.name: 150 m E of Harris Creek
R1C-bear-backcountry-0001.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2017 (9 years old), right here: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
W facing slope, 22 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Harris Creek 150 m W: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

seasonRows.notes: bag 2; Bow Only; no bow only season on the Gulf Islands in MU 1-1 (except Gabriola Island), in zone B of MU 1-5 (Map A12) or on Denman and Hornby Islands (MU 1-6)

plan: Drive: from District of Port Hardy, about 67 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 50.26061, -127.68572, pull off on Access (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: 5.4 km S, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 484 m, about 156 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 220 m SW of the spot at 243 m (50.21301, -127.70768). Water: Harris Creek 70 m NW (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov, Dec (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 1-12, Region 1. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-08-24, closures 2026-10-16.
R1C-bear-backcountry-0001.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 1-12: about 353 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.06 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: more than 5 km from a drivable road. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).
